question: Quality: is B0's judge acceptance not more than 10 points below bare Claude Code's (A)?
issue_selection: scripts/bench/briefed-ab/select_issues.py at this commit over closed issues fetched 2026-10-10: every closed issue (99) fixed by exactly one commit naming only them, 1-20 files, at least one Rust file under crates/, at most 4 crates, 6-1200 changed lines and a diff of at most 100 KB, a body of 80+ characters, excluding S2's 21. That is every qualifying issue the repository has; none is dropped after results.

pins.agent_source: crates/briefed-agent at 6518b03bbd (same source as c34036f3a5), built on the environment
pins.host: oa-dev-env-2 (GCE c3-standard-22 spot, 300 GB): agents, worktrees and builds on one machine (AB_HOST=local), one build checkout, prewarm per issue, incremental builds off, 600 s per command, hidden tests 300 s
pins.login: the owner's Claude Code subscription token from Secret Manager (dev-env-session.sh)

order: issues in a seeded random order; per issue each rep rotates the arm order from a seeded start
outcome: primary: judge_accept = the blind judge (claude-opus-5-5, the JUDGE prompt in ab.py at this commit, issue + merged change + candidate diff, nothing else) scores 4 or 5. Secondary: accepted = judge_accept AND the fix's own tests pass, on the issues whose tests validate (prepare.py --validate, run before any trial).

analysis.primary: difference B0 - A in judge acceptance, mean over issues of per-issue rates, 95% CI from 10000 issue-level bootstrap resamples (seed 11211), reported before cost
analysis.margin: a quality loss of 10 points or more is ruled out when the CI's lower bound is above -0.10. This is a non-inferiority margin; the product spec asks for equal or better, so a result inside the margin but below 0 does not meet the spec's literal gate and is reported as such. Choosing a margin at all is a proposed amendment, flagged here before results.
analysis.sizing: S2's issue-level SD of the judge-acceptance difference was 0.352. With 99 issues the CI half-width is about 0.069; if the true difference is 0, the lower bound clears -0.10 with about 80% power; if it is -0.095 (S2's point estimate) it will not, and the study reports a real loss.
analysis.secondary: strict acceptance on validated issues; cost per accepted (known list prices); median and p90 time; by size (<= 400 vs > 400 changed lines)
analysis.unknown_costs: counted and kept unknown; estimates shown separately
analysis.extension: if inconclusive, a further prospective plan; no post-hoc additions

harness_failures: a trial that hits the login's usage limit is discarded and rerun when the login answers (no outcome was observed); nothing else is rerun or excluded.
